label: Delimiter-biased, token-content-dependent low candidate (no clean rule)
explanation: About 1% of steps. 59% of activation mass is at the <DEL> step, but only 6.6% of <DEL> steps fire, so the step position alone has very low precision. Whether it fires depends on token content in a scattered way. It is more likely when g/x/e come just before (prev_tok or prev2_tok), when the first output is 1/j/a/k/m/p/v, or when the input is r/1/x/y. None of these combinations gets dev F1 above 0.24 (best: <DEL> & out_tok in {1,j,a,k,m,p,v} & g/x/e seen earlier, P=0.27 R=0.21). The rest of the mass is spread over original-phase steps t=1-9 (especially t=2 and t=8-9, inputs r/1/x) and early copy steps. It never fires at t=0. Magnitude is largest at <DEL> and at recall_idx 0-1 steps that output 1. This looks like a distributed code over token identities rather than a single interpretable condition.
